description: Figure 6 illustrates how the number of datasets changes over time for researcher locations, combining the five most frequent locations with an “all other” category, shown as a vertical bar chart. The horizontal axis lists years from 2012 through 2022 in chronological order and is labeled “Year.” The vertical axis is labeled “Number of datasets” and uses a logarithmic scale with tick marks shown at approximately \(10^0\), \(10^1\), and \(10^2\). Multiple colored bars appear for each year, corresponding to the different researcher-location categories indicated by the figure’s legend (five specific locations plus an “all other locations” group); within each year, these bars are placed side-by-side as a grouped arrangement rather than stacked. Bar heights vary by year and category, with early years (around 2012–2015) showing short bars near the \(10^0\) level and later years (especially from about 2016 onward) including taller bars that extend into the \(10^1\) range and, for the tallest category in the latest years, approaching the \(10^2\) level. No bars appear to be specially emphasized with outlines or annotations beyond their distinct colors, and the ordering of years is strictly increasing left to right.
